name: 01_coverage
title: Where the six-year record is complete—and where it is not
caption: Source: v2 primary cohort, 2018–2023. 83,328 recordings after 38 title-year conflicts excluded. Gray = no eligible recording; not zero discussion.

name: 02_theme_changes
title: Which policy phrases became more frequent?
caption: Source: v2; 2022–2023 minus 2018–2019; 273–273 eligible districts. Equal meetings/year/district weighting; pointwise 95% t intervals. Mentions, not stance; panels use different x scales.

name: 03_quarterly_subjects
title: Six subjects across all 24 quarters
caption: Source: v2, 2018–2023; fixed panel of 186 districts with ≥1 eligible recording every quarter. Equal district weight; pointwise district-t 95% intervals; shared shocks not modeled.

name: 04_cleaning_metrics
title: Cleaning changed the topics, but did not improve coherence
caption: Source: completed paired LDA fits; same 83,366 recordings and split, 2018–2023. Shared-reference NPMI; one seed / training pass. Higher values indicate greater coherence or diversity.

name: 04b_perplexity
title: More topics improve prediction within each representation
caption: Source: paired LDA, 2018–2023. Lower is better WITHIN each panel; vocabularies differ, so cross-panel perplexity levels do not measure the effect of cleaning.

name: 04c_topic_matching
title: Some topics survive cleaning; others change substantially
caption: Source: 30-topic paired fits. Forced one-to-one matching is descriptive; low similarity is not evidence of topic equivalence. Food-topic examples include ads; technology examples include repetition.

name: 05_vocabulary_change
title: The vocabulary shift includes policy, pandemic and transcription signals
caption: Source: EARLIER preprocessing, 273 matched districts, 11,804 tested words. Exploratory standardized evidence, not FDR-controlled discoveries. This is not a v2 HC rerun.

name: 05b_global_tests
title: All three global tests detect vocabulary change
caption: Source: earlier pipeline, 2018–2019 vs 2022–2023, 273 districts; 1,999 bootstrap draws. All p values reach 0.0005 floor. Ratios do not rank test power.

name: 06a_coverage_and_voting_maps
title: Geographic coverage and baseline political context
caption: Sources: v2 / NCES 2020 district–county links / Census 2020 boundaries / MEDSL 2016 returns. Contiguous US shown. Gray = no linked observations or missing votes; not zero. County votes are not district or speaker votes.

name: 06b_county_subject_changes
title: Where subject mentions changed in the observed panel
caption: Source: v2 matched-period panel; 2022–2023 minus 2018–2019; mean across linked single-county districts. Contiguous US; gray = no eligible panel district. Different color scales; no population weighting or county-wide representativeness.

name: 06c_state_subject_changes
title: Within-state summaries of the observed district changes
caption: Source: v2, 2022–2023 minus 2018–2019; NCES 2020 state linkage. States with ≥3 panel districts shown. Equal district weight; pointwise t intervals, no adjustment for shared state shocks; not state population estimates.

name: 07_political_context_scatter
title: Do changes differ with the surrounding political environment?
caption: Source: v2 early/late contrasts + MEDSL 2016; 215 single-county districts. Points = districts; OLS mean bands use state-clustered 95% intervals. Unadjusted exploratory associations; not causal or speaker-level ideology.

name: 08_political_trajectories
title: Subject trajectories by pre-period county voting
caption: Source: v2 / MEDSL 2016; 151 linked districts present every quarter, 2018–2023. Fixed groups; equal district weight; 499 within-group state-cluster bootstrap draws, pointwise 95% bands. Descriptive, no covariate adjustment.
